thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected — Elevated 5xx rate on /v1/stream (region: us-west-2). Alert threshold hit (5m rolling). Paging oncall. See: https://monitoring.redwood.com/d/streaming/stream-5xx?orgId=1

oncall-bot: PagerDuty alert sent to #oncall (severity: high). Escalation policy: oncall-engineer -> infra -> eng-sre.

alice: i'm on it, grabbing context. seeing 5xx spike from gateway in the last 3m. new surge ~ 18% 5xx, baseline ~0.3% :grimacing:

bob: logs show a lot of `upstream read timeout` and `chunked decode failed` from gateway proxies. also seeing abrupt `RST` from some downstream clients.

leo: important — a few large customers reported aborted streams and partial payloads. support ticket #S-38921 references `client canceled during stream` and JSON truncation. maria, can you confirm impact?

maria: support-bot pulled customer list: 6 customers with errors > 50 sessions each. one high-value customer (acct: AC-9982) has realtime widgets failing. Their tickets: https://support.redwood.com/tickets/S-38921 and S-38922.

alice: preliminary hypothesis: gateway is hitting per-connection fd/epoll limits under a spike in long-lived streaming connections. that + some chunked-encoding path in proxy causing `unexpected EOF` when clients close mid-stream.

bob: reproducing locally with a simulated client that cancels mid-stream. here's the curl we used: ```bash
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \"https://api.redwood.com/v1/stream\" -d '{\"prompt\":\"stream test\",\"max_tokens\":500}'
# then ctrl-c after first few chunks to simulate client cancel
```

bob: gateway logs (excerpt): ```
[2026-03-15T02:18:12Z] proxy.go:452 upstream read timeout: id=ab12 conn=2034 err=read tcp 10.2.1.4:443: read: connection reset by peer
[2026-03-15T02:18:13Z] http_chunked.go:87 chunked decode failed: unexpected EOF
```

zach: oncall takeover in 10m if we need long-running mitigation. tagging for handoff.

alice: immediate mitigations i'm going to try now: 1) enable gateway soft-throttle on streaming route (reduce new stream accepts by 40%), 2) switch /v1/stream traffic to a lower-concurrency pool (canary hosts), 3) enable aggressive keepalive and adjust proxy read timeout from 60s -> 120s for long polls. will roll sequentially and monitor.

maria: flagged customers and notified CS with suggested workaround: switch to paged API for critical widgets until fixed. CS confirmed customers are experimenting with paged fallback.

deploy-bot: Starting canary deployment: gateway-config v2.14.7 -> v2.14.8-canary (throttle & keepalive). Canary hosts: gw-canary-3, gw-canary-4. Initiated at 02:24 UTC.

leo: adding a temporary rule in route-tier to fallback to non-streaming `paged` route if client signals `prefer_paged: true`. sends 503->200 fallback rather than half-truncated streams.

bob: triage note: interesting pattern — many 5xx have `X-Forwarded-Proto: h2` and larger-than-usual first-chunk sizes. might be a client-side buffering behavior interacting with proxy chunk flushing.

alice: running a quick DD metric query: `avg(last_5m):sum:requests.errors{endpoint:/v1/stream,region:us-west-2,code:5xx} by {host}` — spike concentrated on gw-primary-hosts 6 & 7.

bob: adding a temporary iptables conntrack bump on gw-primary-hosts while canary runs: ```bash
# increase conntrack
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
```

maria: CS update: 4 customers confirmed degraded UX but not full outage; they accepted paged fallback for next 2h. one customer asked for ETA.

alice: can we get a quick health-check of model-serving layer? if gateway is fine the issue might be with fanout to dedicated pools. leo, can you validate KV cache and model shard availability?

leo: model-serving metrics look green. no scaling events. KV cache hit ratio steady. fanout latencies slightly higher but not failing. most 5xx trace back to gateway chunked decode.

zach: i'm taking over active pager. alice handing off: checklist completed in thread, canary deployed, conntrack bumped, customers informed. please post any followups here. :white_check_mark:

alice: handing off notes -> what we changed: throttle 40% on new streams, gateway read timeout bumped to 120s, canary v2.14.8 applied to 2 hosts, conntrack increased. primary mitigation goal: reduce new failing streams and give operators time to root-cause.

support-bot: Incident timeline created: https://incidents.redwood.com/4298765432. Severity: SEV2. Impacted customers: AC-9982, AC-7710, AC-4433, AC-5512, AC-2290, AC-1001.

bob: temp mitigation working — 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 4% on canary hosts inside 8m. monitoring still watching primary hosts.

deploy-bot: Canary health checks passing (3/3). Promoting config to 50% of hosts as progressive rollout.

maria: CS emailed impacted customers with mitigation steps and ETA window ~2-4h for full mitigation. they asked for root-cause and a postmortem.

zach: action items for followup assigned to eng-sre: 1) capture tcpdump on failing sessions (alice), 2) collect full proxy chunking traces (bob), 3) validate keepalive semantics across client libraries and update recommended SDKs (leo), 4) write postmortem and customer-facing blurb (maria).

alice: tcpdump command i used: ```bash
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/stream-fail.pcap host 10.2.1.4 and port 443 and 'tcp[13] & 8 != 0'
```

bob: extracted pcap shows several `FIN` shortly after first chunk and immediate reset from proxy when chunk decoder error occurs. will upload to artifacts. link: https://artifacts.redwood.com/pcaps/4298765432/stream-fail.pcap

zach: leaving a note — if error recurs after config rollout, escalate to kernel/epoll oncall. for now we keep progressive rollout.

alice: great work team. i'll draft a short incident summary and collect logs for the postmortem. tagging eng-sre and infra for full RCA. :memo:

maria: closing loop with support — customers acknowledged workaround. keeping them updated.

oncall-bot: Handoff complete. Current status: mitigated (reduced error rate) — monitoring in progress.

alice: will update incident ticket with timeline and assignments. if anyone sees >5% 5xx persist after 02:50 UTC, ping pager.

zach: taking the oncall until 08:00 UTC. signing out of active triage but will watch alerts. :eyes:

-- end of thread --
